notes_for_editor: Newspaper searches were not completed (Chronicling America queue stalled), so the Nelson/Nilson episode (1907-08), Wilkinson's 1926 death, Ostman's 1942 fall and Burbine's 1943 burns rest on LighthouseFriends (and for Nelson also New England Lighthouses) only; no primary record read. Lighthouse Board reports for 1877-1890 and 1900s are not in the corpus; fog-signal installation 1888 and sector 1889 (LighthouseFriends) were left out. Light characteristic conflicts: the record says Fl G 4s; LighthouseFriends and New England Lighthouses say flashing red; not resolved, left out of facts. Focal height conflicts (NRHP 68 ft 8 in; USLHS 54 ft; record 9.4 m); left out. Automation: both guides say 1953; Wikipedia says 1973 (not used). Designer spelled Elliott by LighthouseFriends and Elliot in most sources; the NRHP OCR is garbled, so the designer is cited to LighthouseFriends. Ship John Shoal: the record puts it in New Jersey, the NRHP says Delaware; the story names it without a state. Keeper roster from the USLHS archive; George Petzolt, John Ostman and others appear at several grades. USLHS roster ends 1949 (Gadbois); LighthouseFriends gives Whitford 1943-44 as the last head keeper before him. Story note: Burbine/Falkner Island and Nelson/Sakonnet links are from LighthouseFriends; Elizur Thompson at Five Mile Point likewise. Fiscal-year notes: the crane was in the FY1891 report; oil house, winch and fog-signal notes are in the FY1892 report; riprap in FY1896; Old New Haven transfer and 30 March 1897 trumpet in FY1897. Printed page numbers were not verified; scan pages cited.
